name: Rice Cereal with Coconut Milk (No Allergens)
description: A naturally allergen-free breakfast using coconut milk (naturally dairy-free) and rice cereal. Perfect for families avoiding all Big 9 allergens. Cross-contact tip: use a clean bowl and spoon not previously used for nuts or other allergens.
steps: Pour rice cereal into a clean bowl (use a dedicated bowl for this person to prevent cross-contact with nuts or other allergens).
Add coconut milk - it's naturally dairy-free and commonly safe for multiple allergen profiles.
Slice banana and add to bowl - bananas are low-allergen and commonly tolerated.
Add a pinch of salt to enhance flavor without allergens.

name: Egg-Free Pancakes (Aquafaba Method)
description: Pancakes made with aquafaba (chickpea liquid) instead of eggs. High in protein, safe for egg allergies. Naturally eggless binding demonstrates how to replace this critical allergen without gums or additives.
steps: Whisk aquafaba for 1-2 minutes until frothy (replaces eggs' binding protein) - be sure your mixer bowl and whisk are completely clean with no previous egg or dairy residue.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt (avoid any flour that was bagged near nuts or processed in shared facilities if serving someone with a severe nut allergy).
Fold frothy aquafaba gently into dry ingredients, then add coconut milk and oil. Don't overmix.
Cook on a lightly oiled griddle until edges look set, then flip carefully. Aquafaba-bound pancakes are more delicate than egg pancakes, so handle gently.
Drizzle with honey after cooking (honey is naturally single-source, safe for most allergen profiles, though avoid if serving infants under 1 year).

name: Tropical Fruit Smoothie (Free of Big 9)
description: A vibrant, naturally allergen-free smoothie using only whole fruits and coconut water. No added proteins from allergenic sources. Safe preparation emphasizes clean blender use.
steps: Clean blender pitcher and blade thoroughly with hot water and soap - no residue from nuts or seeds should remain.
Peel and cube mango (wash skin first to prevent cross-contact).
Dice pineapple (fresh or thawed frozen, both are safe).
Add fruit, coconut water, and ice to blender.
Blend on high for 45-60 seconds until completely smooth. Serve immediately to prevent separation.

name: Seed-Based Granola (Gluten & Nut Free)
description: Crunchy granola using only seeds (sunflower, pumpkin) with no tree nuts or gluten. Coconut oil keeps it naturally dairy-free. A safer base for mixed-allergen families.
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F. Line baking sheet with parchment paper to prevent any contact with sheet oils or residue.
Combine sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, and shredded coconut in a bowl (seeds are inherently safer than tree nuts for allergic families, with lower cross-contact risk).
Warm coconut oil and honey together, stir in cinnamon and salt.
Toss seed mixture with oil mixture until evenly coated.
Spread evenly on prepared sheet and bake for 25 minutes, stirring halfway through. The goal is light golden, not dark (darker = burnt particles that can irritate sensitive mouths).
Cool completely on the sheet (it will crisp further as it cools) before storing in an airtight container to prevent cross-contact with other foods.

name: Egg-Based Frittata (Carefully Portioned)
description: A protein-packed breakfast using eggs (a common allergen) with clear labeling. For families with egg allergies, swap entirely with aquafaba recipe. Emphasizes egg safety in cross-contact situations.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Sauté spinach and mushrooms in olive oil in an oven-safe skillet (cast iron or stainless steel, well-washed) - no non-stick coating that might hold allergen residue.

Whisk eggs in a separate bowl with salt and pepper (use a clean bowl and whisk dedicated to egg preparation if serving someone egg-free at the same meal - do NOT share whisks or beaters between egg and non-egg dishes).
Pour whisked eggs over sautéed vegetables in skillet.
Cook on stovetop for 2-3 minutes until edges start to set.
Transfer skillet to oven and bake for 12-15 minutes until center is set but still slightly jiggly.
Let cool for 2-3 minutes before slicing. Store portions separately from any egg-free household members to prevent accidental cross-contact.

name: Chicken & Rice Bowl (Clean Prep Method)
description: A foundational one-bowl meal built from naturally allergen-free base (rice) with minimal add-ons. Demonstrates proper cross-contact prevention when preparing shared meals alongside allergen-containing dishes.
steps: Cook rice in a dedicated pot used only for rice (prevents cross-contamination if household also cooks rice with soy sauce or sesame oil).
Season and cook chicken on a separate cutting board, using a separate utensil from shared kitchen tools.
Dice carrots on a clean cutting board (separate from the raw chicken board to prevent bacteria and allergen cross-contact).
Steam carrots and peas together in a clean steamer or pot with a small amount of water.
Once all components are cooked, assemble bowl with rice base, top with chicken, then vegetables.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil and sprinkle with salt. Serve on a clean plate that hasn't contacted allergen sources.

name: Chickpea Salad (Fish-Free Protein Alternative)
description: A plant-protein salad for families avoiding fish/shellfish. Chickpeas provide similar protein density without the allergen. Demonstrates how to build substantial meatless meals for avoiding multiple allergens.
steps: Rinse canned chickpeas under clean running water in a dedicated colander - if household also uses this colander for fish, wash thoroughly with hot soap and water first (shells/fish oil can linger).
Dice cucumber, bell pepper, and red onion on a clean cutting board.
Combine chickpeas and vegetables in a bowl that hasn't touched fish, shellfish, or soy products.
Whisk together olive oil, lime juice, and salt in a separate small bowl (clean, allergen-free).
Dress salad and toss gently to combine. The chickpea texture holds well and won't become mushy if prepared ahead.

name: Turkey Lettuce Wrap (No Bread Allergens)
description: A naturally gluten-free lunch using large lettuce leaves as wraps. Eliminates bread allergens (gluten, eggs, soy often in commercial breads). Clean assembly prevents cross-contact with other lunch items.
steps: Wash butter lettuce leaves thoroughly and pat dry with a clean paper towel (lettuce, if not washed, can carry bacteria and pollen cross-contact risks).
Slice tomato and avocado on a clean cutting board not previously used for nuts or fish.
Lay out lettuce leaves as wrap bases.
Layer turkey, tomato, and avocado evenly across leaves.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil and sprinkle salt.
Roll lettuce leaves around filling and serve. This wrap is stable if eaten fresh, but avoid preparing more than 1-2 hours ahead as lettuce wilts.

name: Clear Vegetable Broth Soup (Naturally Allergen-Free)
description: A light, naturally free of all Big 9 allergens. Clear broth (no cream, no stock cubes with soy/sesame) provides a safe base for mixed-allergen families. Vegetables add volume and nutrition without hidden allergens.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot (use filtered or bottled water if tap water quality is questionable in your area).
Chop carrots and celery into uniform small pieces - this ensures even cooking and makes the soup safer to eat if texture sensitivity is a concern for allergic individuals.
Add carrots and celery to boiling water, simmer for 10 minutes.
Add diced zucchini and simmer another 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in fresh spinach and cook 2 more minutes until wilted (fresh spinach is safer than canned, which may have been processed near other allergens).
Season with salt and black pepper. Serve hot. This soup freezes well for up to 3 months in an airtight container - thaw in refrigerator, never at room temperature, to prevent bacterial growth.

name: Grilled Salmon with Lemon (Fish Allergen Clearly Labeled)
description: Fish (salmon) is a common allergen. This recipe labels it prominently and demonstrates safe prep to prevent cross-contact. For fish-allergic families, demonstrates the importance of dedicated prep surfaces.
steps: If preparing fish alongside fish-free meals for another family member: Use a DEDICATED cutting board and utensils for raw fish. Do NOT reuse these for non-fish foods until thoroughly washed in hot soapy water and air-dried.
Pat salmon fillet dry with paper towel (moisture removal prevents steaming and reduces allergen particles becoming airborne).
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Brush salmon with olive oil, sprinkle salt and pepper.
Grill for 5-6 minutes on first side, then carefully flip using a dedicated fish spatula. Grill another 5-6 minutes until flesh is opaque.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over cooked salmon just before serving.
Clean grill grates and utensils immediately after with hot soapy water to prevent fish oil contaminating later meals for non-fish-eating family members.

name: Pasta with Olive Oil & Garlic (Dairy-Free)
description: Pasta with no dairy (no butter, cream, or cheese). Olive oil and garlic provide flavor and richness naturally. Demonstrates building satisfying meatless, dairy-free meals for families avoiding multiple allergens.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil (salt aids gluten activation for proper pasta texture and signals flavor).
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente - do NOT overcook, as mushy pasta can exacerbate swallowing difficulties in some allergic individuals who also have texture sensitivities.
While pasta cooks, slice garlic thinly (thinner slices distribute flavor more evenly and cook more gently, reducing burnt bits that can irritate sensitive GI tracts).
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat, add garlic, and cook gently for 1-2 minutes until fragrant (do NOT brown - browned garlic becomes bitter and harder to digest).
Stir in spinach and cook 1-2 minutes until wilted (spinach shrinks significantly, so start with more than you think you need).
Drain pasta, reserving 0.5 cup pasta water. Add drained pasta to olive oil mixture.
Toss gently, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create light sauce. Finish with red pepper flakes and additional salt to taste.

name: Vegetable Stir-Fry with Coconut Aminos (Soy-Free)
description: Stir-fry traditionally relies on soy sauce (soy is a Big 9 allergen). This version uses coconut aminos - a naturally soy-free, nut-free alternative that provides similar umami depth. Demonstrates allergen substitution strategy.
steps: Cook rice in a dedicated pot (ensures no soy sauce residue from previous meals contaminates this soy-free dish).
Prepare vegetables: cut broccoli into small florets, slice bell pepper into thin strips, trim snap peas. Keep vegetables separate to cook at correct rates.
Heat coconut oil in a wok or large pan over high heat (coconut oil has a high smoke point suitable for high-heat cooking).
Add garlic, stir constantly for 30 seconds until fragrant (prevents burning).
Add broccoli and bell pepper, stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Add snap peas, stir-fry another 2-3 minutes until all vegetables are tender-crisp.
Pour coconut aminos over vegetables (this soy-free alternative prevents cross-contamination for soy-allergic families). Toss everything gently and cook 1 more minute to marry flavors.
Serve over rice. Coconut aminos is lower in sodium than soy sauce, so taste and add a pinch of salt if needed.

name: Turkey Meatballs (Pork-Free, Gluten-Free Base)
description: Meatballs traditionally use breadcrumbs (gluten, often contains egg and soy). This version uses crushed rice cereal as a binder - naturally gluten-free and avoids other common bread allergens. Clearly pork-free for dietary restriction households.
steps: Crush rice cereal into small crumbs (texture should resemble coarse breadcrumbs) and set aside. Rice cereal as a binder is gentler on allergic GI systems than wheat-based breadcrumbs.
Finely mince onion and garlic (small pieces distribute throughout meatballs and ensure even flavor).
Combine ground turkey, rice cereal crumbs, minced onion, garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl using a fork or your hands (minimize overmixing, which toughens the meat).
Form into 1.5-inch balls (consistent size ensures even cooking; too large means raw centers).
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Carefully place meatballs in hot oil and cook 4-5 minutes per side until browned and internal temperature reaches 165°F (measured with a clean meat thermometer to confirm done-ness without cutting, which releases juices).
Transfer meatballs to a paper-towel-lined plate to absorb excess oil. Cool for 2-3 minutes before serving.

name: Vegetable Paella (Shellfish & Fish-Free)
description: Paella traditionally features shellfish (a Big 9 allergen). This version uses hearty vegetables and legumes for protein and texture. Demonstrates building celebratory meals that safely exclude prominent allergens.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or shallow skillet (wide, shallow cooking surface ensures even heat distribution and proper rice texture).
Dice onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes until translucent (translucency indicates proper breakdown, easier digestion).
Add minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Dice bell pepper and tomato, add to pan, cook 3-4 minutes.
Stir in rice, coating grains with oil (this prevents clumping and ensures proper al dente texture).
Add vegetable broth (standard store-bought broth is typically shellfish-free, but if serving someone with shellfish anaphylaxis, verify broth label or make your own).
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Do NOT stir frequently - proper paella requires a slightly crispy bottom layer (socarrat) that forms when rice sits undisturbed.
After 15 minutes, stir in rinsed canned white beans and diced zucchini.

Continue cooking until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed (another 10-15 minutes). Sprinkle saffron on top for color and mild flavor (saffron is a single-source spice, safe for most allergen profiles).
Let rest for 3-5 minutes before serving. This dish is safest eaten fresh; do not store at room temperature longer than 2 hours.

name: Rice Noodle Bowl (Sesame Oil-Free)
description: Asian noodle bowls typically rely on sesame oil (sesame is a Big 9 allergen). This version uses olive oil and ginger for warmth and aromatic depth. Safe for sesame-allergic families wanting Asian-inspired cuisine.
steps: Bring vegetable broth to a boil in a large pot (use a dedicated pot if household also cooks with sesame oil - sesame allergen particles can linger).
Mince ginger and garlic finely (small pieces ensure even distribution and prevent fibrous texture in broth).
Add ginger and garlic to boiling broth, simmer 2 minutes until fragrant (infusing allows flavors to meld).
Add rice noodles and cook according to package directions (usually 3-5 minutes) until tender.
Meanwhile, chop bok choy and julienne carrot.
Add vegetables to broth in the last 2 minutes of noodle cooking (bok choy wilts quickly; carrot's thinness allows quick softening without mushiness).
Stir in olive oil (sesame oil alternative providing richness and the fatsoluble vitamin carrier function) and salt.
Serve in bowls with broth. This dish is best eaten fresh but can be refrigerated and reheated gently.

name: Mango Sorbet (No Tree Nuts, Dairy, or Gluten)
description: A naturally allergen-free frozen dessert using only mango and sugar. No common allergens - truly safe for families managing multiple restrictions. Demonstrates how to deliver a satisfying sweet course without allergen concerns.
steps: Peel and pit mangoes, then cut flesh into 1-inch chunks (uniform size helps blender work efficiently).
Freeze mango chunks in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet for at least 2 hours or overnight (proper freezing ensures true sorbet texture, not icy slush).
Place frozen mango chunks, sugar, lime juice, and salt in a blender or food processor.
Blend on high for 3-5 minutes, stopping to scrape sides as needed (thick consistency requires patience and multiple pulses).
Serve immediately for soft-serve texture, or refreeze for firmer sorbet.
This dessert can be stored frozen in an airtight container for up to 1 week (longer storage allows ice crystals to form, changing texture).

name: Coconut Milk Pudding with Berries (Allergen-Free Dessert)
description: A creamy dessert made with cornstarch thickening (no eggs, no dairy) and coconut milk. All Big 9 allergens avoided through ingredient selection. Demonstrates dessert safety for the most restricted families.
steps: In a small bowl, mix cornstarch with water to form a smooth slurry (prevents lumps that can irritate swallowing).
Heat coconut milk and sugar in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Slowly add cornstarch slurry to hot coconut milk, stirring constantly for 2-3 minutes until thickened (constant stirring prevents cornstarch from clumping).
Remove from heat, stir in vanilla extract.
Pour into individual serving dishes and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set.
Top with fresh blueberries just before serving (fresh berries are lower-allergen than processed; if using frozen, thaw in refrigerator, never at room temperature, to prevent bacterial growth).
Store covered in refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Rice Cereal Treats (Egg-Free, Nut-Free Bars)
description: A crispy snack bar using rice cereal and coconut oil (no marshmallows with gelatin, no eggs, no nuts). Delivers familiar snack satisfaction without allergens. Safe treat for school lunches and travel.
steps: Line an 8x8 baking pan with parchment paper to prevent sticking and allow easy removal.
Warm coconut oil and honey together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring gently (warm, not hot - overheating honey damages enzymes and creates bitter flavor).
Remove from heat and stir in a pinch of salt (enhances sweetness perception).
Add rice cereal and fold gently until evenly coated (avoid crushing cereal - you want crunch).
Transfer mixture to prepared pan and press down firmly with the back of a wooden spoon or greased hands.
Cool completely (at least 30 minutes) before cutting into 9 bars.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.
These bars are shelf-stable and safe for school lunch boxes without refrigeration, reducing cross-contamination risk during transport.

name: Homemade Apple Chips (No Added Sugar or Oil)
description: Crispy, lightly sweet snack made from only apples. No added allergens, no processing. Perfect for between-meal grazing and teaching kids about whole-food snacking. Requires an oven, not special equipment.
steps: Preheat oven to 250°F (low temperature ensures even drying without burning).
Core apples and slice thinly (uniform thickness is critical for even cooking; use a sharp knife or mandoline).
Arrange apple slices in a single layer on parchment-lined baking sheets (parchment prevents sticking and allows air circulation).
Sprinkle lightly with cinnamon (cinnamon has antimicrobial properties and aids digestion).
Bake for 50-60 minutes, stirring halfway through, until edges are golden and chips are dry and crispy.
Cool completely on the baking sheet (residual heat continues crisping). If not fully crisp, return to oven for 10 more minutes.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week (longer storage may allow moisture reabsorption, making chips chewy).
These chips are excellent for teething babies, lunch boxes, and post-meal snacking without allergen concerns.

name: Date & Coconut Energy Balls (Nut & Dairy-Free)
description: No-bake energy bites using dates (natural sweetness) and shredded coconut (natural fat). Nut-free for tree-nut-allergic families, dairy-free for lactose-restricted diets. Stable at room temperature for portable snacking.
steps: Pit dates if using whole dates (pitting removes any fragments that could present choking hazard for young children).
Process dates in a food processor until finely chopped (looks like coarse paste).
Add shredded coconut, coconut oil, vanilla, and salt. Pulse until mixture holds together when pressed (texture indicates proper moisture).
Use a small cookie scoop or your hands to form 1-inch balls (consistent size ensures even composition and portion control).
Chill in refrigerator for 30 minutes (cold makes balls firmer and easier to handle).
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freezer for up to 1 month.
These balls are shelf-stable if kept in a cool bag during travel, making them ideal allergen-free school snacks.

name: Hummus (Sesame-Free Version with Tahini Alternative)
description: Hummus traditionally contains tahini (sesame seeds). This version substitutes sunflower seed butter - a naturally nut-free, sesame-free creamy base that maintains the dip's essence. Teaches allergen-specific ingredient swaps.
steps: Rinse canned chickpeas thoroughly under running water (reduces gas-producing compounds; use a clean colander dedicated to non-seafood use).
Combine chickpeas, sunflower seed butter, lemon juice, and minced garlic in a food processor.
Blend until mostly smooth (some texture is pleasant; completely smooth can feel over-processed).
With processor running, slowly drizzle in olive oil until mixture reaches desired consistency.
Add salt and taste. If too thick, add water by the tablespoon until reaching proper dipping consistency.
Transfer to a serving bowl and drizzle lightly with additional olive oil (serves as both garnish and preservation layer).
Serve with cut vegetables: carrots, celery, cucumber, bell pepper (all vegetables are naturally allergen-free and add fiber).
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Sunflower seed butter oxidizes slightly over time (harmless), but flavor and color are best fresh.

name: Air-Popped Popcorn with Olive Oil (No Butter or Allergen Toppings)
description: Popcorn is naturally allergen-free whole grain, but often gets toppped with butter (dairy), nuts, or soy. This version uses olive oil and salt only - a simple, safe snack for multiple-allergen households.
steps: Use an air popper or a covered pot on the stovetop for popping (air-popped avoids oil cooking at high temperatures, which can create problematic compounds).
If using a stovetop: Heat olive oil in a covered pot over medium-high heat, add popcorn kernels, and shake frequently until popping slows to 2-3 seconds between pops. Pour into a large bowl.
Sprinkle salt evenly over warm popcorn and toss gently to coat.
Serve fresh for best crunch. Popcorn stores in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week but loses crispness over time.
This snack is naturally vegan, gluten-free, and free of all Big 9 allergens - exceptionally safe for schools with strict allergy policies.

name: Frozen Fruit Pops (Dairy-Free, No Added Sugar)
description: Homemade frozen pops using only fruit and its natural juices. No gelatin (animal product), no added sugars, no dairy. A cool, refreshing snack that's completely allergen-free and naturally sweet.
steps: Blend berries and apple juice together until completely smooth (no chunks - chunks can be choking hazards in pops).
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve if desired for perfectly smooth pops, or leave with pulp for extra fiber.
Pour mixture into popsicle molds (fill to about 3/4 inch below rim, leaving space for expansion).
Freeze for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.
If wooden sticks are used, insert them after 1 hour of freezing when mixture is slushy enough for sticks to stand upright but not so frozen that sticks crack the mixture.
Run warm water over mold bottoms to release pops.
Store frozen pops in a freezer-safe bag or container for up to 1 month.
These pops are ideal for teething relief and provide hydration during hot weather without allergen risk.

name: Sweet Potato Toast with Avocado (Gluten & Egg-Free)
description: Thick-sliced sweet potato replaces bread (eliminating gluten and eggs in commercial breads). Topped with creamy avocado and fresh herbs. Demonstrates how to re-engineer breakfast favorites for allergy safety.
steps: Wash sweet potato thoroughly (residue from soil can harbor cross-allergens or bacteria).
Slice sweet potato lengthwise into 0.5-inch-thick slabs (consistency is important for even cooking).
Toast slices in a toaster oven at 400°F for 10-12 minutes until slightly softened and lightly browned at edges (regular toasters may not fit thick slices; toaster ovens provide more control).
Meanwhile, cut avocado in half, remove pit, and scoop flesh into a small bowl.
Mash avocado with lime juice, salt, and black pepper (lime prevents browning and adds brightness).
Spread mashed avocado on warm sweet potato toast.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil and garnish with fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately. This is best consumed fresh, as sweet potato toast softens if made in advance.

name: Lentil Patty (Gluten-Free, Protein-Rich)
description: Lentils provide complete plant protein. Bound with rice flour (gluten-free) instead of breadcrumbs. A substantial burger for vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free diets. Cross-contact note: use dedicated cookware if serving alongside allergenic foods.
steps: If using canned lentils, rinse thoroughly under clean water (reduces gas-producing oligosaccharides and prevents cross-allergen residue).
Finely mince onion and garlic (small pieces distribute throughout and ensure even flavor).
Roughly mash cooked lentils with a potato masher (texture should be chunky, not pureed - maintains structural integrity during cooking).
Combine mashed lentils, rice flour, minced onion and garlic, chopped herbs, salt, and pepper.
Form into 4 patties of equal size (uniform size ensures even cooking; use a burger press for consistency or shape by hand and pack firmly).
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook patties 4-5 minutes per side until browned and crispy (don't flip too early; a golden crust helps hold the patty together).
Serve on lettuce leaves (to avoid cross-contact with gluten if household also uses bread) or gluten-free bread if available.
These patties can be frozen raw on a baking sheet and cooked later, making them convenient for quick meals.

name: Quinoa & Vegetable Power Bowl (Complete Protein)
description: Quinoa is a complete plant protein with all 9 amino acids. This bowl layers it with colorful vegetables. Safe for vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free diets simultaneously. All Big 9 allergens naturally excluded.
steps: Rinse quinoa under running water in a fine-mesh sieve for at least 1 minute (removes saponins, a naturally occurring compound that can cause GI upset).
Bring 2 cups water to a boil, add rinsed quinoa, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed and quinoa is tender.
Remove from heat, let rest 5 minutes covered, then fluff with a fork (resting allows proper moisture absorption).
Meanwhile, dice bell pepper and cucumber, halve cherry tomatoes, and rinse canned black beans (all on a clean cutting board dedicated to allergen-free preparation if sharing kitchen space).
Transfer cooked quinoa to a bowl and stir through warm (allows vinaigrette absorption).
Add vegetables and black beans.
Whisk together olive oil, lime juice, cilantro, and salt. Drizzle over bowl and toss gently.
Serve at room temperature or chilled. This bowl is excellent for meal prep and stores covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Roasted Root Vegetables with Herbs (Simple, Hearty)
description: A satisfying vegetable-forward dinner where roasting caramelizes natural sugars, creating richness without fats or allergens. All Big 9 allergens absent by design. Perfect side or main for restricted diets.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F (high heat ensures proper caramelization without drying vegetables).
Wash vegetables thoroughly with produce brush under running water (especially important for root vegetables with soil residue).
Peel vegetables and cut into uniform 0.75-inch chunks (size consistency ensures even cooking - pieces too large remain raw inside; too small burn on outside).
Toss vegetables with olive oil, torn fresh herbs, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Spread in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet (single layer allows roasting, not steaming).
Roast for 30-35 minutes, stirring halfway through, until vegetables are tender inside and caramelized (browned, not burnt) on edges.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot.
Leftovers store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and can be reheated gently.

name: Baked White Fish with Lemon (Fish Allergen Clearly Marked)
description: Fish is a Big 9 allergen and is clearly labeled here. For fish-allergic families, this demonstrates proper prep isolation. For fish-tolerant families, it shows a simple preparation. Emphasizes cross-contact prevention protocols.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Place fish fillet on parchment paper on a baking sheet (parchment prevents contact with sheet surfaces that may have fish oil residue from previous meals).
Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, pepper, and dill.
Squeeze lemon juice over fillet.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.

Important: If preparing fish alongside fish-free meals for another household member, use SEPARATE serving utensils, cutting boards, and cookware. After cooking, clean all fish-contact surfaces immediately with hot soapy water.
Serve immediately.

name: Chickpea Curry with Coconut Milk (Soy & Sesame Free)
description: Curries often use soy sauce and sesame oil. This version uses coconut milk for creaminess and excludes soy/sesame entirely. Demonstrates how to adapt favorite cuisines for allergen safety.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions in a dedicated pot (prevent sesame oil cross-contamination if household also makes sesame rice).
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Dice onion and cook 3-4 minutes until translucent (translucency indicates sugars have begun caramelizing).
Add minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant (prevents browning, which tastes bitter).
Stir in curry powder and cumin, cook 1 minute to bloom spices (blooming releases flavor compounds through dry-heating in fat).
Add coconut milk and rinsed chickpeas (use a dedicated colander for chickpeas if household uses it for shellfish).
Simmer for 10 minutes until flavors meld.
Stir in fresh spinach and cook 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt to taste. Serve over rice.
This curry stores well; flavors improve after a day. Reheat gently on stovetop with a splash of water if needed.

name: Applesauce Cookies (Egg-Free, Dairy-Free, Nut-Free)
description: Cookies leavened by baking soda (in reaction with applesauce acid) instead of eggs. No dairy butter. No nuts. Demonstrates how baked goods can be safety-engineered for multiple allergen profiles.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (moderate temperature prevents bottoms from burning while centers cook).
Cream together melted coconut oil and sugar in a bowl (if not melted, use a mixer to thoroughly combine).
Stir in applesauce and vanilla (applesauce replaces egg's moisture and binding function while adding natural sweetness).
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.
Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients until just combined (overmixing develops gluten, resulting in tough cookies).
Drop spoonfuls onto parchment-lined baking sheets.
Bake 12-14 minutes until centers are set but tops are still slightly soft (residual heat continues baking after removal from oven).
Cool on baking sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Green Juice (No Added Nuts or Allergens)
description: Fresh green juice focusing on leafy greens and mild fruits. No added proteins from nuts. No sweeteners. A nutrient-dense beverage for families managing multiple allergens and valuing whole-food nutrition.
steps: Wash spinach thoroughly in a clean colander (spinach can harbor soil and bacteria; multiple rinses ensure safety).
Chop celery into 2-inch pieces to fit through juicer or blender.
Core apple and cut into chunks (seeds contain small amounts of cyanogenic compounds; removing seeds is safer).
Cut lemon in half (seeds optional but can be bitter if included).
Peel ginger (unpeeled ginger can be harsh on sensitive stomachs).
If using a juicer: Process all ingredients, then add water and stir.
If using a blender: Blend all ingredients until completely smooth, then strain through a fine-mesh sieve or nut milk bag if a cleaner texture is preferred.
Drink immediately (oxidation begins within minutes after blending; nutrients degrade over time).
This juice is best consumed fresh but can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours in an airtight container.

name: Baked Sweet Potato with Cinnamon (Naturally Allergen-Free)
description: A naturally sweet, starchy snack or light meal. No toppings with allergens. The sweet potato's natural creaminess satisfies without butter or other allergens. Teaches simple, whole-food snacking.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash sweet potato thoroughly under running water with a produce brush (removes soil that may harbor allergen cross-contamination).
Pierce with a fork in several places (allows steam to escape evenly, preventing explosion).
Place directly on oven rack on a baking sheet below to catch any drips (direct heat circulation ensures even baking).
Bake 35-45 minutes depending on size (pierce center with a knife to check - should slide through tender flesh with no resistance).
Remove carefully (skin is very hot) and cut open lengthwise.
Fluff interior flesh with a fork to release steam.
Sprinkle cinnamon and a pinch of salt over top.
Serve immediately. The natural sugars concentrate during baking, creating sweetness without added toppings.
Leftover baked sweet potato can be refrigerated and reheated gently or used in smoothies.

name: Rice Water Drink (Electrolyte Replacement, Allergen-Free)
description: Rice water has been used for centuries to support digestion and hydration, especially beneficial for those recovering from GI upset. Pure carbohydrates and electrolytes without any allergens. Safe for all restricted diets.
steps: Bring 3 cups water to a boil in a clean pot (use filtered water if possible to ensure purity).
Add rice and reduce heat to low, simmering for 15 minutes until rice is very soft and water is starchy.
Strain rice through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, keeping the liquid (discard cooked rice or repurpose for animals).
Stir salt into rice water (salt replaces electrolytes lost through illness).
Optional: stir in honey for a touch of sweetness and additional carbohydrate energy. Avoid if serving to infants under 1 year.
Drink warm or at room temperature, sipping slowly if recovering from GI upset (small, frequent sips are gentler than large gulps).
Store refrigerated for up to 2 days. Reheat gently if preferred warm.
This drink is particularly valuable for individuals with multiple allergens who have limited food options during recovery from foodborne illness.
